title: The Telescope That Shared Its Time
title_ja: 観測時間を分け合う望遠鏡
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度・観測は架空の思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果や観測施設の運用規則ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine an international research consortium operating a hypothetical telescope capable of collecting observations that would be difficult to obtain through smaller instruments available to its individual members.
sentences.ja: 各会員が使える小型機器では得にくい観測を集められる仮想望遠鏡を運用する国際研究連合を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Because the time available for observations is limited, the consortium invites research teams to submit proposals explaining what they hope to discover and why the telescope is particularly suitable for their investigations.
sentences.ja: 観測時間が限られるため研究チームに何を発見したいか、なぜ望遠鏡が特に適するかを説明する提案書を出すよう求める。

sentences.en: A committee is responsible for comparing these proposals and distributing access to the instrument in a manner that advances scientific knowledge without making participation depend exclusively on the resources of particular institutions.
sentences.ja: 委員会は特定機関の資源だけに参加を依存させず科学知識を進歩させる形で提案を比較し機器への利用時間を配分する責任を負う。

sentences.en: The committee initially considers ranking every proposal according to the expected importance of its results, but several members question how confidently such importance can be assessed before the relevant observations have been made.
sentences.ja: 当初成果の予想重要性で順位づけを考えるが、観測前に重要性をどの程度確信を持って評価できるか疑問視する委員がいる。

sentences.en: Their disagreement reveals a fundamental difficulty in distributing a scarce scientific resource among projects whose potential benefits may become apparent only after they have been given an opportunity to proceed.
sentences.ja: 対立は実施機会を得て初めて潜在利益が明確になるかもしれない研究間で希少科学資源を配分する根本的困難を示す。

sentences.en: Several proposals describe investigations that could extend previous work by obtaining more detailed measurements of phenomena that are already relatively well understood.
sentences.ja: 複数の案は既に比較的理解されている現象のより詳細な測定値を得て以前の研究を発展させる調査を述べる。

sentences.en: Other proposals involve exploratory observations for which the researchers cannot specify a narrow range of expected outcomes, although they can explain why the information might raise scientifically valuable questions.
sentences.ja: 他の案は科学的に価値ある問いが生じ得る理由は説明できても予想結果の狭い範囲は指定できない探索的観測を含む。

sentences.en: The committee recognizes that requiring identical kinds of predictions from both groups might favor projects with established methods while reducing opportunities to investigate unfamiliar possibilities.
sentences.ja: 両群に同じ種類の予測を求めれば確立手法を持つ研究が有利になり未知の可能性を調査する機会が減り得ると認識する。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the members also agree that uncertainty alone cannot justify allocating valuable observation time to a proposal that lacks a coherent research question or a credible explanation of how the resulting data would be examined.
sentences.ja: それでも不確実性だけでは一貫した研究課題やデータをどう検討するかの信頼できる説明を欠く提案への貴重な観測時間配分を正当化できないと合意する。

sentences.en: The challenge is therefore to evaluate the quality of the reasoning appropriate to each kind of investigation rather than treating the predictability of its results as the sole measure of scientific merit.
sentences.ja: 課題は成果の予測可能性を科学的価値の唯一の尺度とせず調査の種類に適した推論の質を評価することだ。

sentences.en: A second difficulty concerns the institutions submitting proposals, since research teams differ considerably in their previous access to comparable instruments and their experience preparing formal applications.
sentences.ja: 別の難しさは同等機器の過去の利用経験や正式申請の準備経験が研究チームによって大きく異なるため提案を出す機関に関係する。

sentences.en: A carefully written application may demonstrate important planning skills, but its persuasive presentation might also reflect access to established networks of specialists who have helped the team develop its proposal.
sentences.ja: 丁寧な申請書は重要な計画技能を示しても説得的な提示には提案作成を助けた専門家の既存ネットワークへのアクセスも反映されているかもしれない。

sentences.en: Conversely, an application containing an interesting scientific idea may fail to provide sufficient technical detail because the team has had few opportunities to become familiar with the telescope's particular capabilities.
sentences.ja: 逆に興味深い科学的発想を含む申請も望遠鏡固有の能力に慣れる機会が少なく十分な技術的詳細を提供できないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The committee considers offering general guidance and a preliminary opportunity to clarify technical questions before the final submission deadline, making the same information available to all applicants.
sentences.ja: 最終提出期限前に一般的指針と技術的問いを明確にする予備機会を提供し全応募者が同じ情報を得られるようにすることを検討する。

sentences.en: This arrangement would not guarantee equal success, nor would it remove the need to reject proposals that could not be implemented with the available equipment and resources.
sentences.ja: この仕組みは同等の成功を保証せず利用可能な機器と資源で実施できない提案を却下する必要をなくすわけでもない。

sentences.en: The committee also considers whether allocating all available observation time at the beginning of a research period would prevent the consortium from responding to unexpected developments later in the year.
sentences.ja: 全観測時間を研究期間の初めに割り当てると年の後半の予想外の展開に対応できなくなるかも検討する。

sentences.en: Reserving a portion of the schedule could preserve opportunities to investigate discoveries that had not been anticipated, although doing so would reduce the time immediately available to projects that had successfully completed the ordinary selection process.
sentences.ja: 日程の一部を確保すれば予想外の発見を調べる機会を維持できるが、通常選考を通過した研究が直ちに使える時間は減る。

sentences.en: Rather than assuming that reserved time is necessarily wasteful or necessarily valuable, the members propose defining the conditions under which such time could be released for additional observations.
sentences.ja: 確保時間が必ず無駄または有用と想定せず追加観測に時間を割り当てられる条件を定義する案を出す。

sentences.en: They also consider recording the reasons for allocation decisions so that later reviewers can examine whether the procedures supported the consortium's stated objectives under the circumstances in which the decisions were made.
sentences.ja: 後の審査者が決定時の事情において手順が連合の明示目的を支えたか調べられるよう配分理由の記録も検討する。

sentences.en: The committee acknowledges that the eventual scientific success of a particular project would provide useful information for future reviews without proving that every decision made during the original selection process had been appropriate.
sentences.ja: 特定研究の最終的科学成功は将来の見直しに有益な情報を与えるが元の選考の全判断が適切だったとは証明しないと認める。

sentences.en: This fictional example does not describe the actual allocation procedures of any existing astronomical observatory; instead, it illustrates broader tensions that arise when institutions must distribute limited opportunities for inquiry under conditions of uncertainty.
sentences.ja: この架空例は実在の天文台の配分手順を述べるのでなく不確実な状況で限られた研究機会を配分する機関に生じる広い緊張関係を示す。

sentences.en: A selection process may need to consider scientific feasibility, the diversity of questions being investigated, and the availability of opportunities for researchers to acquire the knowledge necessary to participate effectively.
sentences.ja: 選考は科学的実現可能性、研究課題の多様性、効果的に参加するための知識獲得機会を考慮する必要があるかもしれない。

sentences.en: These objectives cannot necessarily be combined into a single numerical ranking without making contestable judgments about their relative importance.
sentences.ja: 相対的重要性について議論の余地のある判断をせずにこれらの目的を単一の数値順位にまとめられるとは限らない。

sentences.en: A defensible allocation process should therefore make its priorities and practical limitations sufficiently explicit for participants to understand how decisions are reached and where opportunities for improvement remain.
sentences.ja: 正当化可能な配分手続きは参加者が判断方法と改善の余地を理解できるよう優先事項と実務限界を十分明示すべきだ。

sentences.en: The value of a shared telescope depends not only on the quality of the instrument itself but also on the institutional arrangements through which researchers are given meaningful opportunities to ask questions that the instrument might help them answer.
sentences.ja: 共有望遠鏡の価値は機器自体の質だけでなく機器が答える助けとなり得る問いを立てる実質的機会を研究者に与える制度にも依存する。

vocabulary.definition: quality of being able to be predicted
act of giving something for review
able to be supported by reasons

questions.prompt: Why must the consortium compare proposals?
options: The telescope cannot collect any data.
Every team is required to use identical instruments.

questions.prompt: What makes expected importance difficult to rank?
options: All proposals describe results already verified.
Potential benefits may emerge only after research begins.
The committee has access to every future observation.
Scientific importance is determined solely by institutional size.
questions.explanation_ja: 研究前には価値を確定しにくい。

questions.prompt: Why might identical prediction requirements disadvantage exploratory work?
options: Exploratory researchers are prohibited from submitting proposals.
All exploratory work lacks scientific reasoning.
Such work may generate valuable questions without narrowly predictable results.

questions.prompt: What does the committee say uncertainty alone cannot justify?
options: Providing a rationale for an exploratory question.
Allocating time to a proposal without coherent reasoning.
questions.explanation_ja: 根拠のない配分を正当化できない。

options: Guarantee equal selection results for all teams.
Reduce differences in access to technical application knowledge.
Allow experienced institutions to decide alone.
questions.explanation_ja: 申請機会の条件を改善。

questions.prompt: What is not guaranteed by the arrangement?
options: Access to the same general guidance.
An opportunity to clarify technical questions.
questions.explanation_ja: 結果の平等は保証しない。

questions.prompt: What is the trade-off involved in reserving time?
options: Lower telescope quality versus greater accuracy.
More applications versus no scientific observations.
Flexibility for unexpected findings versus immediate access for selected projects.
Equal success versus identical research interests.
questions.explanation_ja: 予備時間と通常配分の間の選択。

questions.prompt: Why record the reasoning behind allocations?
options: Prove that every successful result arose from perfect selection.
Replace technical data with personal preferences.
Enable reviews of whether decisions served stated goals under their actual conditions.
questions.explanation_ja: 当時の判断根拠を検討。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Fair and useful allocation of scarce research time requires explicit, evidence-informed trade-offs among multiple objectives.
Scientific merit can always be captured in a single score without value judgments.
Every exploratory project should be funded before established research.
The quality of shared instruments alone determines opportunities for discovery.
questions.explanation_ja: 複数目的と制約の明示。

grammar.focus: why the telescope is particularly suitable

grammar.explanation_ja: while＋分詞による同時性と対比。

grammar.focus: nor would it remove the need

grammar.explanation_ja: althoughは譲歩、doing soは予約時間の確保。

paraphrases.source: Because the time available for observations is limited, the consortium invites research teams to submit proposals explaining what they hope to discover and why the telescope is particularly suitable for their investigations.
paraphrases.rewrite: Teams must explain their aims and why this instrument fits their research.

paraphrases.source: The committee recognizes that requiring identical kinds of predictions from both groups might favor projects with established methods while reducing opportunities to investigate unfamiliar possibilities.
paraphrases.rewrite: Uniform prediction requirements could favor established approaches at the expense of exploratory ones.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同一基準の異なる影響。

paraphrases.source: This arrangement would not guarantee equal success, nor would it remove the need to reject proposals that could not be implemented with the available equipment and resources.
paraphrases.rewrite: Guidance neither ensures equal acceptance nor eliminates rejection of infeasible proposals.

paraphrases.source: Reserving a portion of the schedule could preserve opportunities to investigate discoveries that had not been anticipated, although doing so would reduce the time immediately available to projects that had successfully completed the ordinary selection process.
paraphrases.rewrite: Holding time in reserve enables responses to unexpected findings but leaves less time for initially selected proposals.

discourse.role_ja: 探索的研究を認めても根拠は必要。
申請経験と発想の対照。
予備枠の価値を条件付きで検討。
実在の制度でなく一般的課題。

cloze.explanation_ja: 議論の余地がある判断。
